rows.name: MMLU
rows.status: Saturated (\~92%+ frontier), contaminated; replaced by MMLU-Pro then GPQA/HLE

rows.name: MMLU-Pro
rows.status: Saturating at frontier; still useful mid-tier

rows.name: GPQA Diamond
rows.status: Saturated at the frontier (Astra 96.0%, Muse Spark 1.3 94%); dropped from the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index as saturated, Sep 2026. Still separates the 60-90 band.

rows.name: AA-Briefcase
rows.measures: Agentic knowledge work, private test set
rows.status: Active; added to the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.2 (Sep 2026) as one of GPQA Diamond's two replacements

rows.name: GDP.pdf
rows.measures: Long-context document reasoning across 4,592 PDF pages
rows.status: Active, nowhere near saturation (GPT-6 Astra 33.2%, GPT-5.6 Sol 28.2%, Claude Fable 5.1 26.2%)

rows.name: HLE (Humanity's Last Exam)
rows.status: Active headline benchmark; \~46% no-tools SOTA, 55-65% with tools; known errata (see deep dive)

rows.name: SimpleQA
rows.format: Open QA; correct / incorrect / not attempted

rows.name: GSM8K
rows.status: Saturated (\>95%) and heavily contaminated; GSM-Symbolic showed template overfit

rows.name: AIME (yearly)
rows.status: Active as a rolling set; each vintage saturates within \~1 yr (AIME'24-'25 near-solved)

rows.name: HMMT / MathArena
rows.measures: Fresh competition math, evaluated at contest time

rows.name: FrontierMath
rows.status: Active at upper tiers; base tiers \~89% SOTA, Tier 4 v2 is the frontier

rows.name: LiveCodeBench
rows.status: Active; frontier \~90%+ on recent windows, saturating

rows.name: Codeforces rating evals
rows.status: Active; frontier models at grandmaster-level ratings

rows.name: SWE-bench (full/Lite)
rows.status: Superseded by Verified; contamination and solution-leak issues

rows.name: SWE-bench Verified
rows.status: Saturating (\~97% SOTA); headline moved to SWE-bench Pro

rows.name: SWE-bench Pro
rows.measures: Harder, contamination-guarded repos; public + private splits
rows.status: Active headline coding-agent benchmark (\~59-80% depending on split/scaffold). Superseded as the hard target by SWE-Bench Pro v2 below, so a "SWE-bench Pro" figure now needs its major version as well as its split and harness.

rows.name: SWE-Bench Pro v2
rows.measures: Repository-level issue resolution, 642 tasks drawn from 11 repositories
rows.status: Active and deliberately unsaturated: the strongest models reach only about 23% on the public set. Built because SWE-bench Verified went soft, and the reported failure shape is the useful part, since smaller models collapse specifically on multi-file scenarios rather than degrading evenly, which is a residual an evaluation should decompose rather than average.

rows.name: SchrodingerRepo
rows.measures: Whether a repository-level coding score survives removing familiar repository cues
rows.format: Paired % resolved and interaction cost, on dynamically transformed repositories
rows.status: Active, and a method rather than a leaderboard. Four behaviour-preserving transformations at evaluation time (problem-statement reconstruction, namespace remapping, intra-file layout reordering, functionality-preserving rewriting) consistently degrade agent performance and raise interaction cost on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-QA, with exploration and localisation the dominant cost drivers. The aggregator that surfaced it records a 6 to 14 point gap; the abstract states direction rather than a figure.

rows.name: Terminal-Bench 1.0/2.0/2.1/4.0
rows.measures: End-to-end tasks in a terminal sandbox
rows.status: Active; 4.0 is current (Sep 2026: recalibrated task resources, task fixes, saturated tasks removed). Claude Opus 5.5 66.4%, GPT-6 Astra 57.9%, Claude Fable 5.1 55.8%, Claude Opus 5 52.3%, Grok 4.7 38.0%. 2.x scores are not comparable to 4.0, so a 2.x figure quoted beside these is a false comparison rather than an old one.

rows.name: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1
rows.measures: Research workflows in a terminal sandbox: 70 expert-curated tasks across five science domains
rows.status: Active and still the least saturated agent headline, but only just, and the rate is the finding: a 30.0% top score at launch in Aug 2026 (Claude Opus 5), 52.6% a week later (Claude Fable 5.1), and 64.6% for GPT-6 Astra as reported on Anthropic's own Opus 5.5 comparison table, where Opus 5.5 itself reaches 58.7%. 34.6 points of headroom in roughly seven weeks. 0.2 in development

rows.name: Real-SWE
rows.measures: Licensed tasks from real companies' private production repositories
rows.format: % resolved over scored rollouts, each model in its native harness
rows.status: Active; contamination-proof by licensing rather than by recency. Fable 5.1 leads at 38.8%, roughly 20 points below the same models' Terminal-Bench 4.0 scores

rows.name: Phi-Bench
rows.measures: Whether a model can build the AI infrastructure it runs on: kernels, multi-file repositories, end-to-end optimisation
rows.format: % of 85 tasks passed across nine categories

rows.name: OSWorld / OSWorld-Verified / OSWorld 2.0
rows.status: Active but nearing saturation. Three names are in circulation and they are not one scale: the original, the Verified revision that exists because roughly 300 tasks or checkers were broken, and OSWorld 2.0, which is what current vendor cards report. On OSWorld 2.0: Claude Opus 5.5 81.8%, Claude Opus 5 74.0%, GPT-6 Astra 72.6%, GPT-6 Sol 60.5% offline at extra-high effort. A figure quoted without which of the three it came from carries no information.

rows.name: tau2-bench
rows.measures: Dual-control user + agent, telecom domain added; 2026 update adds voice and retrieval

rows.name: Hyper-tau-bench (Sierra)
rows.measures: Agents that build agents, working alone against paired with an engineer
rows.status: Active; Claude Opus 5 at maximum reasoning passes 23.9% alone against 82.2% paired, a 3.4x gap on identical work

rows.name: AutomationBench 1.0.6
rows.measures: Agent workflows across 47 tools, reported with cost per task
rows.format: Task success plus dollars per task
rows.status: Active and far from saturation. GPT-6 Sol 33.2% at high effort for \$0.27 per task, Claude Opus 5 26.9% at roughly nine times the cost. One of the few suites whose headline pairs a score with a price, which is what makes a cost claim checkable at all. The unversioned "AutomationBench" figures recorded elsewhere in this knowledge base have not been matched to a version, so do not quote them in the same breath as these.

rows.name: Agents' Last Exam
rows.status: Active, young, single reported figure: GPT-6 Sol 56.4% at maximum effort. Nothing independent yet, so treat the number as a vendor card entry rather than a leaderboard position.

rows.name: MCP-Universe / MCPMark / MCP-Bench
rows.measures: Tool use through real MCP servers
rows.status: Active, young; see agentic deep dive

rows.name: GDPval-AA v2.1
rows.measures: Economically valuable occupational tasks, Artificial Analysis variant of GDPval
rows.status: Active; Claude Opus 5.5 1846, Claude Opus 5 1708, GPT-6 Astra 1542. Note it is a different instrument from the OpenAI-run GDPval above, with its own version number, and the Elo scale means only differences are meaningful.

rows.name: MOLE
rows.measures: Whether a monitor catches agent harm: 150 AI-operated accounts sharing nine stateful services over 30 simulated workdays
rows.format: Harm-completion rate and monitor detection rate
rows.status: Active; the subject of measurement is the monitor, not the agent

rows.name: Emergence World
rows.measures: Persistent multi-agent worlds run for 16 days under three adversarial stress tests
rows.status: Active; the only entry here whose episodes do not end, which is what lets it see drift and compounding failure

rows.name: EdgeBench
rows.measures: 51 agent tasks reporting cost per hour alongside success
rows.format: Success rate plus cost per hour
rows.status: Active; one of the few suites that can express an efficiency result at all

rows.name: HarnessDev
rows.measures: Whether an LLM can create its own agent harness and then evolve it from feedback
rows.format: Downstream task success and execution-token cost over 2,207 instances
rows.status: Active; generated harnesses trail human-engineered ones on code and search, match them on writing and ML experimentation, and evolution gains transfer poorly

rows.name: Vals AI Legal Research Bench
rows.measures: Legal research correctness on a validation set
rows.status: Active and index-sensitive: 54% with a licensed legal index against 38.7% with web search on identical weights

rows.name: ARC-AGI-1
rows.status: Solved at frontier (o3, late 2024); prize track retired. Now cheaply reproducible: 44% from a small transformer trained from scratch for roughly 67 cents (Sep 2026)

rows.name: ARC-AGI-2
rows.status: Rapidly saturating through 2026 (high-60s to low-90s depending on leaderboard, from \~4% in early 2025)

rows.name: ARC-AGI-3
rows.status: Active, but harness-dominated: humans 100%; bare or default-harness SOTA \~30%, rising to 95.5% (Prime Agent) and 100% (Nvidia AVO) with a research harness (Aug 2026). Since Sep 2026 ARC Prize publishes two labelled harnesses per model: GPT-6 Astra 62.7% standard provider-agnostic, 99.9% Provider Adapter. Always report the harness.

rows.name: SimpleBench
rows.measures: Trick/commonsense questions where humans beat LLMs

rows.name: NIAH / MRCR / Fiction.liveBench
rows.measures: Needle retrieval; multi-round co-reference; long narrative
rows.status: NIAH saturated (marketing only); MRCR and Fiction.liveBench active

rows.name: IFEval
rows.status: Saturating but still standard on model cards

rows.name: LMArena (Chatbot Arena)
rows.status: Active but critiqued (Leaderboard Illusion); frontier cluster \~1510-1525

rows.name: ImageNet (ILSVRC)
rows.measures: Image classification; started the deep-learning era
rows.status: Retired as a frontier target; still a reference staple
